newsitem.title: CHINA: Widow of China's ex-president to auction antiques.
newsitem.headline: Widow of China's ex-president to auction antiques.

text.p: The widow of China's former president Liu Shaoqi, who was deposed and died in prison during the chaotic 1966-76 Cultural Revolution, is to auction her private antique collection, her daughter said on Friday.

Wang Guangmei, 75, would donate proceeds from the November 12 auction to an anti-poverty fund that she heads, her daughter Ting Liu, vice-chairman and president of Sungari International Auction Co, told reporters.

Her collection, consisting of porcelain bowls and plates and an ivory brush holder from the Qing (1644-1911) and Song (960-1279) dynasties, is estimated to be worth between 341,000 and 510,000 yuan ($41,000 and $61,000).
"She's pushing me almost every day. She wants to make (a) donation...(but) she doesn't have money," the daughter said.

The antiques were Wang's dowry from her wealthy father, who was a vice-minister of commerce and industry in the republican government, which overthrew the Qing dynasty in 1911 but was defeated by Chairman Mao Zedong in 1949.
Wang's antiques were seized when she was jailed in the Cultural Revolution, but the authorities returned some of her collection when she was released from prison 11 years later.
Her husband was jailed and died in prison in 1969. President Liu Shaoqi was rehabilitated posthumously in 1980.
